maya: Heads-up — ember-int8 canary is showing a subtle new class of funcall parse failures. Not classic trailing-comma; more like truncated escape sequences and half-formed unicode escapes (\uXXXX cut off).

trent: Hmm. That's odd. Is it correlated with sequence length or a particular prompt family?

maya: So far it's concentrated on prompts that produce long JSON arrays (tool list + metadata). FP16 mirrors are at 0.2% parse fail, ember-int8 at 1.6% on 5k samples. Example snippet from canary out (trimmed):```..., \"tools\": [ { \"name\": \"write\", \"args\": [ \"log.txt\", \"error at line 42: \\\"Unexpected token \\\\u\" ] } ]``` You can see the escape cut at the unicode \u.

olga: That smells like a tokenization id shift plus batch boundary cut where the model emits a backslash sequence that spans token boundaries and a final token gets dropped. Did we change BPE merges or vocab ordering in this quant build?

maya: Quant recipe is per-channel symmetric (v2.7) + a new vocab packing step. I ran a quick tokenization diff on 100 prompts and the id sequences diverge in ~0.6% of positions, mostly at high-unicode regions.

trent: Could also be runtime-side: our int8 fast-path coalesces certain UTF-8 outputs into micro-chunks; if a trailing micro-chunk is elided by CB or KV-cache trimming, you get half-escapes.

sasha: Can you repro with a no-CB, no-kvcache mirror? If failure drops it's an interaction, not pure quant. Also try streaming vs non-streaming outputs.

maya: Repro command I used:```for i in $(seq 1 5000); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"ember-int8","prompt":"<funcall-heavy-unicode>","max_tokens":400}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq -r '.out' >> out.log; done; grep -E '\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{0,3}$' out.log | wc -l``` That returns the number of likely truncated unicode escapes.

ci-bot: Canary ember-int8 rolled to 20% at 2912345400 — https://deploys.redwood/2912345400 (auto-alert threshold: 0.5% parse)

olga: I spun a no-CB mirror and a fp16 mirror. No-CB mirror dropped to 0.4%, fp16 at 0.18%. Streaming off vs on also changed pattern: streaming produced more partial-escape suffixes.

trent: Signal looks strong for a batching/streaming interaction with the int8 emission path. Short-term mitigations: 1) reduce ember-int8 canary to 5% and enable fp16 mirror, 2) enable soft-parse NDJSON fallback (line-delimited repair) at proxy for canary routes, 3) add tokenization boundary simulator to int8 onboard checks (simulate escaping sequences across token splits).

maya: I'll open a canary-hold and attach sample traces + token-id diffs. Also propose disabling the new vocab packing step for the next quant build to isolate.

sasha: Agreed. Long-term we should add an onboard unit that runs a set of stress prompts with high-unicode, multi-tool arrays, and both streaming/non-streaming settings. If int8 passes those, it can graduate.

deploy-bot: Canary ember-int8 scaled back to 5% at 2912345700 (actioned by @sasha).

maya: Update (15m): no-CB + streaming-off mirror dropped truncated-escape hits to 0.25% on 2k samples. NDJSON soft-repair reduces customer-facing failures to 0.08%. Filing incident doc now. Thanks all. :+1:
